name: onewrite_recall_v1
purpose: One-write persistent causal memory channel in frozen Qwen3-1.7B-Base (Codex direction round 15): E writes a 16-d state from a single-fact source ('the private tag of {name} is {tag}'); J adds it ONCE at block 12 to the final token of the 'Internal record:' slot; ~50 tokens of unrelated filler and an unseen query wording follow; the endpoint is the raw decoded tag. A positive licenses only a persistent causal memory channel - not abstraction, transfer, native state, or latent mathematics.
source_templates_train: The private tag assigned to {name} is {tag}.
Registry note: {name} carries the private tag {tag}.
For the record, the tag filed under {name} reads {tag}.
source_templates_eval: Archive slip. Entity {name}; private tag on file: {tag}.
Catalogue entry for {name} lists the private tag {tag}.

wordings.B: Registry lookup. Tag on file for {name} =

valid_line:
VALID TAGS: fask | nimb | ruzz | pelt | gorm | twyl | hesk | vorn
ANSWER WITH ONE VALID TAG ONLY.
fillers:
Internal record:
The registry office keeps its ledgers in a locked cabinet on the second floor of the old annex. Each morning the clerk on duty checks the seals, initials the daily sheet, and files any new slips that arrived overnight. Requests for lookups are handled strictly in the order received, and the answer is written on a single line of the reply form.
Internal record:
Before noon the archive room is quiet except for the steady ticking of the old brass wall clock. The junior assistant sorts the incoming post into three small wooden trays, stamps each item with the date, and carries the sealed envelopes across to the reading desk. Any query about a filed item is answered briefly, with the reply entered on one line.
design_note: Round 16 (2026-08-29) locked amendments: 8 tags (chance 0.125), fixed VALID TAGS line in every target, two fixed fillers >= 64 tokens within 2 tokens of each other, both heldout source phrasings x both target wordings (64 cases), wrong-state = same entity with a counterfactual tag (balanced derangement) under the same source wording, write at the slot's final token, byte-identical nonvisible target across arms, zero-hook must reproduce cue row-for-row else INVALID.
amendment_r17: Round 17 (2026-08-29): cue completion is a diagnostic with no minimum (pre-lock and locked); completion >= 0.95 required in write, wrong, random and visible arms; if random-write completion fails the construction is FAIL not PARTIAL; zero-hook must reproduce cue raw text, choice and completion row-for-row else INVALID - NO VERDICT. The round-16 validation stands recorded as a formal failure of its original gate.
